why: The answer depends on lichens being the pioneer community of primary (xerarch) succession on bare rock, because they alone can secrete acids that dissolve rock into soil, which mosses, liverworts and algae need before they can establish.
note: The chapter choice is right - NCERT teaches ecological succession inside the Ecosystem chapter - but the supplied topic list covers only productivity, decomposition, energy flow, food chains, trophic levels, pyramids, ecosystem services, nutrient cycling and ecosystem structure. None of those teaches succession, and this chapter has no 'Unspecified Topic' row either, so 'unsure' plus a named gap is the only honest answer. The same gap already swallowed 2015_A q122 (succession definition).
proposed_topic: Ecological Succession (Primary and Secondary, Hydrarch and Xerarch, Pioneer and Climax Community)
